newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BIRZHU MILK SAYS H1 97 NET PROFIT 2 MLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: BIRZHU MILK SAYS H1 97 NET PROFIT 2 MLN LITAS.

text.p: Lithuania's Birzhu Milk said on Tuesday that its audited net profit for the first half of 1997 was 2 million litas compared to 1.5 million litas in the same period in 1996.
The company also said that it will not reach its target of 13 million litas net profit in 1997 because of the government's decision to raise milk prices from August 1.
The company forecast last week that its net profit for the first half of 1997 will fall between 2.5 and 3 million litas.
"The audit excluded from our profit account around 500,000 litas of our consumers debts stemming back from 1994," the company's director general Vladas Songaila told Reuters.
Songaila also said that the government's decision to increase milk buying prices from August 1 was an expensive blow to the firm.
"The government's unexpected decision when we had the contracts with our clients signed already will reduce our annual profit by around 3 million litas," Songaila said.
The firm planned a 13 million litas net profit for 1997.

He also said that the new production lines scheduled to start operations at the beginning of the month were delivered later than expected but did not say how much the delay might reduce the 1997 profit.
The firm reported earlier that its sales in the first half of 1997 were 51.2 million litas.
Birzhu Milk is one of the three corporates on the Vilnius bourse's elite five member official list.
